clips.title: The story
paras: 'An Enticing Offer' is a local initiative aimed at repelling encroaching murlocs using bait concocted from toxic duskweed. By harvesting the noxious weed directly from nearby farmland, the plan simultaneously assists local growers and establishes a deterrent against shoreline pests.

Dealing with pervasive murloc infestations often calls for inventive pest control rather than endless frontline skirmishes. 'An Enticing Offer' proposes a clever solution to address two local nuisances in a single stroke: crafting a specialized bait laced with duskweed to deter murlocs from encroaching onto settled lands, while clearing encroaching weeds from neighboring crop fields in the process.

The core ingredient of the concoction is duskweed, a persistent wild weed that plagues nearby agricultural plots. In substantial quantities, the petals of duskweed contain potent toxins harmful to most beasts. By gathering the weed directly from troubled farmers, the fields are purged of an aggressive pest plant, while its toxic harvest provides the necessary base to train murloc packs to steer clear.

While the resulting concoction is relatively simple to prepare, duskweed's indiscriminate toxicity makes handling it somewhat hazardous. Domestic animals and pets must be strictly kept away from the finished mixture, and the quest giver offers a parting caution to ensure that local acquaintances, namely someone named Jason, do not mistake the pungent bait for a meal.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: I've got a few ideas on how to deal with murlocs. And one of those also helps some others in the process.

There's a weed often found on farms in the area called duskweed, and in large quantities the petals are toxic to most animals. If we make some murloc bait with the plant, hopefully that can train those creatures to stay away.
And some farmers get their fields cleared in the process. Truly a win-win... Truly a win-win.

clips.title: Completion
paras: It's pretty simple bait, but as long as nobody's pet gets into it, it should be safe. Just tell Jason not to eat any of it.
